title: Design Review: Onboarding Flow v2
overview: 38% of new signups drop off at the calendar connection step because they haven't seen any value yet.
Onboarding v2 leads with a sample meeting, then upload or paste; calendar connection becomes an optional third step.
In usability tests 4 of 5 people completed the new flow, compared with 2 of 5 for the old one.
Fixes before launch: a skip option, a progress bar, clearer upload errors and WCAG AA button contrast.
The flow ships behind a feature flag as a 50/50 A/B test, measured on 7-day activation.

comments.body: Can we get this drop-off broken down by signup source?

transcript: Sofia Alvarez: Thanks for coming. Today I want feedback on version two of onboarding. I'll share my screen. The short version is that we lose too many people before they ever see a transcript.
Sofia Alvarez: Right now thirty eight percent of new signups drop off at the calendar connection step. They don't trust us with their calendar before they've seen any value.
Emily Watson: That lines up with support tickets. People ask why we need calendar access before they've done anything.

Sofia Alvarez: So the new flow flips the order. Step one, you see a sample meeting with a real transcript, summary and action items. Step two, you upload a recording or paste a transcript. Calendar connection becomes step three, and it's optional.
Jordan Rivera: I really like leading with value. What does the sample meeting look like?
Sofia Alvarez: It's a fake product sync with three speakers. You can click around the transcript, play it, and see the summary update. We highlight three features with small tooltips.
Ravi Patel: From an engineering point of view, the sample meeting is easy. We can ship it as static data, so no backend work is needed.
Emily Watson: One concern. If calendar connection is optional, will people forget to do it? Most of the long term value comes from the bot joining meetings automatically.

Sofia Alvarez: Good point. We'd remind them after their first uploaded meeting is processed, when they've already seen the value. The prompt says something like, want this for every meeting automatically?
Jordan Rivera: That's a much better moment to ask. I'd also add a progress indicator so people know how many steps are left.
Sofia Alvarez: Yes, I tested that. In the usability sessions, people with a progress bar were more likely to finish. Let me show you the results.
Sofia Alvarez: We ran five sessions. Four out of five people completed the new flow without help. With the old flow, only two out of five did.
Emily Watson: That's a big jump. What tripped up the one person who didn't finish?
Sofia Alvarez: The upload step. They had a video file that was larger than our limit, and the error message just said upload failed. They didn't know what to do next.
Ravi Patel: We can fix that easily. I'll show the file size limit up front and add a clear error message that says the file is too large and suggests compressing it or pasting a transcript instead.
Jordan Rivera: Can we also add a skip option on step two? Some people just want to look around first.
Sofia Alvarez: Agreed, I'll add a skip link that takes them straight to the dashboard with the sample meeting pinned.
Ravi Patel: One more thing from my side. The purple text on the light purple buttons fails the contrast check. We should fix that before we ship anything.
Sofia Alvarez: Good catch. I'll update the button colors so they meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio.
Jordan Rivera: How do we want to roll this out? I'd rather not switch everyone at once.
Ravi Patel: We can put it behind a feature flag and do a fifty fifty A B test. The flag system already supports percentage rollouts.
Emily Watson: If we A B test, let's measure activation at seven days, not just completion of the onboarding flow. Completing onboarding doesn't help if they never come back.
Jordan Rivera: Agreed. Primary metric is seven day activation, meaning they processed at least two meetings. Secondary metric is onboarding completion.
Sofia Alvarez: Great. So I'll finalize the designs with the skip option, the progress bar and the new button colors by Friday.
Ravi Patel: And I'll start building behind the feature flag next week, starting with the sample meeting and the upload error handling.
Emily Watson: I'll write the help center article for the new flow and brief the support team before the test starts.
Jordan Rivera: Perfect. Let's target starting the A B test in two weeks. Thanks Sofia, this is a really strong piece of work.
